logs: A/B miner calibration on 18 goinfusive-com tiles

sonnet run done: 54 raw cards, 30 accepted, ~36225 out tokens

raw_cards.claim: The hero deploys three distinct weight levels — bold display for the primary headline, spaced caps for the subhead label, and regular-weight body — but the mid-tier subhead ('WE HANDLE EVERYTHING:') fights the headline rather than supporting it, because its all-caps tracking reads nearly as loud as the display text above it.
visible_tells: Bold mixed-case headline at ~60px
All-caps spaced tracking on subhead at similar visual weight
Regular-weight sentence case body below at much smaller size

raw_cards.claim: The CTA button ('UNLOCK YOUR GROWTH POTENTIAL') and the trust-line beneath it ('Trusted By Leading Wellness Clinics Nationwide') are correctly sized relative to each other — button label sits mid-hierarchy and the trust line drops to a clearly subordinate small weight — showing deliberate size stepping at the bottom of the hero.
visible_tells: Button label in caps at readable mid-size
Trust line in noticeably smaller regular weight below

raw_cards.page_or_region: homepage profit-leaks section (bottom of tile-00, top of tile-01)
raw_cards.claim: The section heading ('Uncover the Hidden Profit Leaks…') repeats the hero's bold display size and purple-on-dark colour treatment without reduction, so the page never visually steps down from hero pitch to supporting content — every section screams at equal volume.
visible_tells: Large bold two-line heading in the same colour and weight as the hero headline
No visible size reduction from hero to this section head

raw_cards.claim: The brand name 'INFUSIVE' in large spaced caps functions as a section heading, followed by a purple italic subhead and then regular body paragraphs — three levels are present and distinguishable — but the spaced-caps treatment is decorative rather than informational, making this feel like a logotype dropped mid-page rather than a section anchor.
visible_tells: 'INFUSIVE' in large tracked caps acts as H2
Purple italic line below as subhead
Regular-weight body paragraphs beneath

raw_cards.claim: This section shows the clearest three-level hierarchy on the homepage: a large regular-weight question as the H2, a medium bold statement as H3, and small regular labels on the feature cards below — each level is visually distinct and proportionally stepped.
visible_tells: Large light-weight question headline at top
Smaller bold subtitle beneath
Small sentence-case card labels at bottom tier

raw_cards.claim: Within a single heading, multiple weight and style treatments are applied ('The Only', 'Built For Wellness Clinics', 'By Industry Insiders') creating fragmentation rather than hierarchy — the eye has no single anchor and the sentence must be re-read to parse the intended stress.
visible_tells: Three weight/style variants within one heading span
Bold and regular alternating mid-sentence without a structural break

raw_cards.claim: The three-card step section ('Apply / Onboard / Grow') uses a consistent card-heading weight and matching body-copy size, which is internally coherent — but the section-level heading 'How It Works' barely differs in size from the card titles, compressing the scale and reducing the sense of entry into a new content zone.
visible_tells: 'How It Works' heading not substantially larger than card-level 'Apply', 'Onboard', 'Grow' labels
Card body copy at same apparent size as section intro

raw_cards.claim: The newsletter block achieves the site's clearest hierarchy in a small area: a bold display heading ('Stay Ahead of the Chaos'), a medium-weight subtitle ('Join the Infusive Insider Newsletter'), a small regular descriptor line, and even smaller bulleted body — four readable levels in one compact zone.
visible_tells: Bold display heading at largest size
Semi-bold subtitle one step smaller
Descriptor and bullet body at clearly smaller regular weight

raw_cards.claim: The sticky tab bar ('Seamless Ordering & Vendor Control', 'Direct Pharmacy Integration', etc.) uses white regular-weight text on purple with no size differentiation between the active and inactive tabs — the typographic system provides no visual feedback about position in the content, forcing the reader to read every label to locate themselves.
visible_tells: All tab labels at identical size and weight
No bold, underline, or size shift on the active tab
Tab bar text occupies same visual rank as body copy below it

raw_cards.page_or_region: platform page feature sections (Inventory Management System)
raw_cards.claim: Feature sections follow a repeating H2 + italic H3 + body pattern that is legible, but the italic subhead ('Know exactly what you have. Use every dollar wisely.') sits so close in size to the H2 that differentiation relies almost entirely on italics alone — a fragile distinction especially at small viewport sizes.
visible_tells: H2 and italic H3 differ by only a few pixels in apparent size
Differentiation collapses to italic vs. roman with minimal size step

raw_cards.claim: The closing 'Built for Wellness. Designed for Scale.' block correctly uses a large bold display line, a smaller regular-weight explanatory sentence, and a clearly subordinate italic tagline below — three levels that step down cleanly and read well over a dark background.
visible_tells: Large bold heading at top
Smaller regular body sentence in the middle
Smallest italic summary line at bottom

raw_cards.page_or_region: platform page body copy over photography
raw_cards.claim: Where body copy sits against a desaturated photography bleed (the vendor ordering section), white regular-weight text at small size has insufficient contrast against the mid-tone grey image areas — legibility relies on luck of the background crop rather than any typographic or overlay decision.
visible_tells: Small regular white body text against mid-grey photographic background
No scrim, vignette, or background-lock visible behind the paragraph text

raw_cards.page_or_region: platform page 'What You Get with Infusive' tab section
raw_cards.claim: The 'What You Get with Infusive' section heading is displayed in a clean, moderately-sized semi-bold treatment that stands above the tab row — this one instance where the section label genuinely outranks the navigation below it — but the gap to the tab bar is so tight that the heading reads almost as part of the interface rather than an editorial section marker.
visible_tells: Section label 'What You Get with Infusive' in semi-bold above tabs
Minimal vertical breathing room between label and tab bar compresses the hierarchy

raw_cards.claim: The hero arranges headline, product screenshot, and testimonial card in a loose three-element composition that works at a glance, but the floating quote card clips awkwardly against the screen mockup with no deliberate overlap logic.
visible_tells: testimonial card overlaps laptop mockup without clear z-layer intention
center-weighted headline above a left-aligned screenshot creates mild axis tension

raw_cards.page_or_region: Homepage — logo marquee / social proof bar
raw_cards.claim: The partner logo strip is single-row and runs off the right edge with no fade or containment, producing a visually broken strip rather than a polished carousel or contained grid.
visible_tells: logos bleed past the right viewport edge with no gradient mask
mixed logo sizes — some large wordmarks next to small icons — creating uneven visual weight

raw_cards.claim: The inline name/email + CTA form is neatly contained in a single horizontal row, but the section below it switches to a hard left-aligned large wordmark and body copy with no shared left margin discipline between the two zones.
visible_tells: form inputs and CTA button are flush and consistent in height
the 'INFUSIVE' all-caps block below starts at a noticeably different left inset than the form above it

raw_cards.claim: The before-state layout places a video/image panel on the left and a clean vertical stack of four icon-plus-label cards on the right, with consistent internal padding and even inter-item spacing across all four rows.
visible_tells: four pain-point rows are identically spaced with icon, text, and right-border all aligned
left panel and right stack share a common vertical midpoint

raw_cards.page_or_region: Homepage — product feature split with laptop mockup
raw_cards.claim: The two-column benefit-card flanking arrangement around a centred laptop mockup is a recognisable SaaS pattern executed competently, but the background bleed from a previous section (blurred figure) sits unresolved behind the laptop, muddying the composition.
visible_tells: purple/blue background photographic bleed visible behind left and right benefit cards
benefit cards use rounded-rect containers with consistent padding but differ slightly in text density

raw_cards.claim: The four-up outcome icon grid inside the light card maintains uniform column widths, equal icon sizes, and consistent caption alignment, making it the tightest component on the homepage.
visible_tells: four columns are evenly distributed with no ragged right edge
icon, bold label, and body text in each column share identical vertical rhythm

raw_cards.claim: The three numbered step cards share a consistent rounded-rect shell and equal widths, but card 2 ('Onboard') renders significantly taller than cards 1 and 3, breaking the horizontal baseline alignment.
visible_tells: card 2 bottom edge sits lower than cards 1 and 3
step number badges are consistent but the photo heights inside each card differ

raw_cards.claim: The vendor logo wall uses two rows of logos at wildly inconsistent sizes with no normalisation to a common optical height, making the grid read as an unedited dump rather than a curated partner display.
visible_tells: 'Baxter' wordmark is roughly 3x the visual weight of adjacent logos like 'McGuff'
rows have different numbers of logos causing visual imbalance between row 1 and row 2

raw_cards.claim: The newsletter section pairs a decorative book mockup with a benefit list and form in a two-column layout, and the internal rhythm is clean, but the book graphic and text column are not vertically centred against each other.
visible_tells: book mockup sits higher than the midpoint of the text block beside it
form fields and CTA button align consistently at the same height

raw_cards.claim: The persistent horizontal feature-tab navigation appears twice in the same tile — once as a full-width purple band and once partially shown below as a redundant repeat — suggesting the sticky bar and a static instance are stacking without proper z-index or layout containment.
visible_tells: two identical tab bars visible within the same viewport slice
second instance appears cropped at the bottom edge, confirming an overlap or duplicate render

raw_cards.page_or_region: Platform — feature detail sections (Ordering / Pharmacy / Inventory)
raw_cards.claim: Each feature section follows the same two-column pattern (body copy left, screenshot right) giving the page predictable rhythm, but the split proportions shift between sections — sometimes 40/60, sometimes closer to 50/50 — undermining the grid's authority.
visible_tells: Ordering section shows a narrow text column beside a wide screenshot
Pharmacy Integration section shows text and image at near-equal widths in the adjacent scroll position

raw_cards.claim: The 'Built-In 797 Compliance' four-card icon row is the most precisely constructed component on the platform page: uniform card widths, a common icon size and position, and headline copy that breaks consistently across all four.
visible_tells: four rounded-rect cards share identical width and internal top-padding
icon placement is pixel-consistent in each card's upper region

raw_cards.claim: Content density is inconsistent: sections with large data-table screenshots crowd the viewport edge while adjacent text-only sections have generous whitespace, with no consistent outer margin or content-width container holding the two treatments to the same width.
visible_tells: table screenshot extends nearly edge-to-edge of the tile
text column beside it has substantial left padding that does not match the table's left edge

raw_cards.claim: The footer CTA reuses the same newsletter layout block (book mockup + form) from the homepage without adaptation, producing a competent but clearly templated repeat rather than a purposefully designed page-specific close.
visible_tells: identical two-column book-plus-form block appears in both the homepage footer and here
same body copy cadence and button style, confirming a component paste rather than a new composition

raw_cards.claim: The brand commits to a narrow deep-purple-to-violet palette and holds it consistently across the hero background, nav bar, and primary CTA button, establishing clear palette discipline from the first visible pixel.
visible_tells: Dark near-black purple fills the entire hero background
Nav and logo sit on the same dark purple field with no contrast bleed
Primary CTA 'Apply Now' uses a bright magenta-pink accent that is the only warm departure — one controlled accent, not a scattered rainbow

raw_cards.claim: The hero uses a bespoke animated-wave graphic in purple and violet rather than a stock photo or generic gradient, giving the brand a distinct, owned visual texture.
visible_tells: Layered translucent wave forms rendered in purple-to-pink tones fill the right two-thirds of the hero
The graphic is clearly rendered/generative rather than a photograph or off-the-shelf vector pack

raw_cards.claim: The same wave-mesh graphic reappears as a full-bleed CTA band, demonstrating that the bespoke texture is treated as a repeating brand asset rather than a one-off hero flourish.
visible_tells: Purple mesh/wave graphic fills the mid-page CTA band identically in character to the hero
Magenta-outlined pill button is reused verbatim from the hero accent

raw_cards.claim: The three step-cards use recognisable stock clinic photography (smiling professional in scrubs at a desk, video-call screen, group consultation) that is contextually on-theme but visually generic and not shot-to-match the purple brand palette.
visible_tells: Card 1 shows a woman in blue scrubs at a desk — standard healthcare stock framing
Card 2 shows a laptop video-call — generic tech-meets-health composition
Card 3 shows a group meeting in natural daylight — warm tones that sit outside the purple system

raw_cards.claim: The founder photo is a real, natural-light portrait placed on the purple brand background, which partially integrates it, but the image has an assembled feel (cutout figures, no colour grading to match the palette) rather than a purpose-shot brand image.
visible_tells: Two men photographed against a light background, appearing composited onto the dark purple section
No purple tone-mapping or duotone treatment applied to the portrait — it reads as a lifted headshot

raw_cards.claim: Background photography of clinic staff leaks through as a faded dark overlay, blending with the purple palette reasonably well, but the technique (dark-overlay-on-stock-photo) is a common shortcut rather than a considered brand image choice.
visible_tells: Desaturated photo of people looking at a device visible through heavy dark overlay in left portion
The same Acer laptop prop visible in adjacent section confirms this is a pool of generic tech/clinic imagery

raw_cards.claim: The horizontal feature-tab navigation uses the magenta-pink accent as the active-state color and dark purple as the inactive field, demonstrating that the two-tone accent system is wired into interactive UI chrome, not just decorative surfaces.
visible_tells: Active tab ('Direct Pharmacy Integration') is rendered in vivid magenta-pink on white text
Inactive tabs are dark-purple-on-white, completing a controlled two-state system

raw_cards.claim: The vendor logo marquee renders partner logos in their native mixed black-and-white form against the dark purple background without any colour-normalisation treatment, producing a visually inconsistent strip that breaks palette discipline.
visible_tells: McKesson, Baxter, Wells Pharmacy, and others appear in raw black/dark logotype — some near-invisible on the dark ground
No white-knockout or tinted treatment applied to unify them

raw_cards.claim: A stock photo of a clinician looking stressed in a supply-room is used to illustrate the 'before' pain state; the image reads as lifted stock (standard healthcare frustration pose) rather than a curated brand shot, though it is appropriately thematic.
visible_tells: Professional in white coat with hand on head surrounded by shelves of medical supplies — textbook 'stressed clinician' stock composition
A 'Before' label is overlaid to contextualise its use

raw_cards.claim: The newsletter 'book' mockup uses the purple-to-pink gradient system as its cover treatment, extending the palette to a physical/product asset rather than reserving it for screen surfaces only.
visible_tells: Book cover shows purple-to-magenta gradient with white text — matching the site's primary palette exactly
The 'Infusive' wordmark appears on the cover, anchoring it as a brand artifact

raw_cards.claim: Icon illustrations in the compliance feature tiles use a mixed treatment — some are outlined in purple/magenta, some appear closer to neutral grey — without a visually consistent icon color system.
visible_tells: Four feature icons visible across the compliance row show variation in saturation and stroke weight
No uniform tint or backdrop shape unifies them as a set

raw_cards.claim: Section dividers use a custom curved/pointed shape cutout in the brand purple rather than a flat horizontal rule or simple gradient fade, showing that the brand system extends to micro-layout transitions.
visible_tells: Top of tile shows a downward-pointing chevron-style purple shape cutting into the white section below
The same motif appears at the bottom of the tile entering the next purple section

raw_cards.claim: Embedded product-UI screenshots show a predominantly white/grey admin interface that sits in hard contrast to the surrounding deep-purple brand surfaces, with no attempt to frame or tint the UI to soften the disconnect.
visible_tells: White-background data table screenshot placed against the dark purple page background creates an abrupt light island
No device-frame colour treatment or shadow blending is applied to ease the transition

raw_cards.claim: Background photography of a clinician working with a patient is desaturated and overlaid with dark purple, which is a consistent technique across the site but is so uniformly applied that it flattens visual interest and makes all background photography interchangeable.
visible_tells: Section background shows a near-silhouette image of two people — the purple overlay is heavy enough that the figures are barely distinguishable
The same dark-overlay treatment used in at least three other sections produces visual monotony rather than variety

raw_cards.claim: The four problem-state icons (vendor accounts, pricing, allocation, disruptions) share a consistent outline-circle framing and stroke weight, but the glyphs inside are generic stock-library shapes with no custom character.
visible_tells: circular purple border is uniform across all four icons
inner glyphs (chain-link, price tag, grid, globe) are recognizable stock shapes with no site-specific design
stroke weight and fill color are consistent — system exists but is not distinctive

raw_cards.claim: The four benefit icons (growth chart, shield/peace, handshake, clock) use the same framing system as the problem row above, maintaining visual rhythm, but all four glyphs are recognizable off-the-shelf metaphors with no custom illustration.
visible_tells: identical circular outline treatment carried across rows
hockey-stick chart, handshake, and clock are among the most ubiquitous SaaS icon metaphors
no evidence of a custom-drawn icon set — frames are the system, not the glyphs

raw_cards.claim: The four compliance-feature icons (document, clipboard, training badge, audit report) reuse the same circular-outline shell with generic clip-art glyphs, and at this smaller render size the inner detail collapses to unreadable blobs.
visible_tells: icons appear at roughly 40–48px apparent size and inner shapes are indistinct
clipboard and document glyphs are interchangeable at this scale
no visual differentiation between the four concepts beyond label text

raw_cards.claim: The sticky-nav tab icons serving as section labels are rendered at a size where they become illegible decorations, undermining their function as wayfinding anchors.
visible_tells: icons in the horizontal tab bar are approximately 16px apparent size
individual glyphs cannot be distinguished from one another in the tab strip
active-tab icon is indistinguishable from inactive icons except by color of label text

raw_cards.claim: The laptop product render in the hero is cleanly composited with a perspective-matched UI screenshot inside the frame, giving it the appearance of a deliberate product mockup rather than a raw flat screenshot.
visible_tells: laptop frame is dark and proportionally credible
UI screenshot inside tracks the screen angle — no obvious keystone warp or misalignment
overall mockup reads as intentional product photography replacement, not a stock device image with mismatched content

raw_cards.claim: A second laptop mockup in the homepage hero contains a recognizable UI screenshot and a floating testimonial card, but the compositing has soft edges and the product UI at this resolution is too small to evaluate as a design asset.
visible_tells: laptop device frame is present and color-matched to the purple palette
testimonial card floats to the right and is legible
UI content inside the laptop is a data table rendered too small to assess craft

raw_cards.claim: The three process steps replace icon illustration entirely with stock photography thumbnails inside rounded-rectangle cards, a choice that avoids the icon quality problem but provides no iconography craft evidence at all.
visible_tells: cards show photos of a nurse at a desk, a video-call screen, and a clinic team — all stock imagery
no custom icon or illustration represents the Apply/Onboard/Grow steps
numbered circle badges (1, 2, 3) are the only graphic mark, styled as plain filled circles

raw_cards.claim: The 'Stay Ahead of the Chaos' book-cover mockup is a simple purple rectangle with typeset text — no custom illustration, pattern, or graphic element distinguishes it as designed collateral.
visible_tells: book cover is a flat purple-to-pink gradient with white type only
no illustration, icon, or texture appears on the cover face
the mockup itself (three-quarter-view book with shadow) is the only graphic craft here

raw_cards.claim: The inventory section uses small UI-screenshot panels as illustration rather than icons or diagrams, which is a reasonable product-page convention but produces graphic elements that are too small and low-contrast to read as intentional data visualizations.
visible_tells: two mini UI panels show tabular data and a chart but at ~120px width the content is unreadable
no annotation or callout overlays help decode what the screenshots show
the panels are not framed or highlighted — they blend into the dark background

raw_cards.claim: The eight-feature grid (Seamless Ordering through Aligned Patient Care) deploys the same circular icon system as the homepage, confirming a deliberate cross-page icon grammar, though glyph quality remains generic.
visible_tells: icons appear in purple-bordered circles matching homepage style exactly
eight slots use the same shell — system is consistent, not accidental
glyphs visible include a shopping-cart, integration symbol, and bar-chart — all stock metaphors

raw_cards.claim: The reporting section shows a laptop with a data table screenshot but no custom chart graphics, diagram, or annotated visualization — the data promise is not backed by illustrated evidence of the reporting experience.
visible_tells: laptop screen shows a plain tabular list with row data, no charts
a small circular highlight (magnified detail) appears around a cell but adds no clarity at this resolution
no sparklines, bar charts, or trend graphics appear in the section claiming 'Insight-Driven Reporting'

raw_cards.claim: A wide data-table screenshot stands in for any diagram or illustration of the financial integration feature, and at this render width the table rows are unreadable text, providing no visual evidence of the product's analytical sophistication.
visible_tells: table spans nearly full width but text in rows is ~8px apparent size
no callouts, highlights, or annotations direct the eye to meaningful data
section heading promises 'real-time financial visibility' but the illustration is a raw data dump

raw_cards.claim: The wave/mesh network graphic used as a section-break background (visible in the CTA divider) is a recognizable stock 3D particle-mesh asset, not custom illustration, but it is consistently applied as a brand atmosphere element across sections.
visible_tells: purple particle-wave spans full width behind the CTA
the same waveform appears in the homepage hero and at least one additional section divider
asset reads as a purchased or downloaded 3D render — no unique visual signature

rejected_cards.reason: CTA-vs-trust-line size-stepping card (typography, strong) flatters generic competence — a button bigger than a trust line is baseline, no distinctive tell. Cut.

'INFUSIVE' brand-section three-level card (typography, mixed) overlaps the kept profit-leaks and INFUSIVE-left-margin cards; its 'logotype dropped mid-page' read is interpretive with no verifiable hierarchy failure. Cut as low-value.
Redundant with kept typography_03 for the same 'Is your clinic ready' section — would duplicate without a new tell. (This is the strong three-level card, kept; the duplicate framing is dropped.)

'How It Works' heading-vs-card-title compression card (typography, mixed) is a faint, hard-to-verify size claim; the section's clearer issue (card photo heights) is already captured in layout_05. Cut to avoid weak duplication.
Italic-H3-too-close-to-H2 card (typography, mixed) rests on a 'few pixels' distinction not reliably verifiable in the tile; speculative ('fragile at small viewport'). Cut.
White-text-on-photo contrast card (typography, mixed) — body copy in this tile sits on solid purple, not on the photographic bleed; the cited legibility failure is not visible. Reject.
'What You Get with Infusive' section-label card (typography, mixed) — the tight-gap-to-tab-bar claim is interpretive and the label/tab relationship is already covered by the kept tab-bar cards. Cut.
Lead-capture-form left-margin card (layout, mixed) — the claimed differing left inset between form and 'INFUSIVE' block is not clearly visible; both read as centered/near-aligned. Weak tell, reject.
Laptop-flanked benefit-card split card (layout, mixed) — the 'unresolved background bleed muddies composition' is a soft taste read; the SaaS-pattern observation flatters competence. Cut.
Newsletter book-vs-text vertical-centering card (layout, mixed) — minor alignment nitpick, lower value than the kept reuse and logo-wall cards on the same/adjacent tiles. Cut.
Feature-section split-ratio-shift card (layout, mixed) — the 40/60-vs-50/50 claim spans non-adjacent scroll positions and is not verifiable within one tile. Reject.
Section-density inconsistency card (layout, poor) — overlaps the kept color_08 light-island observation on the same tile and is a vaguer container-width claim. Cut as duplicative.
Bespoke-wave-graphic standalone card (color, strong) merged into kept color_02, which covers the wave in both hero and CTA band. Redundant alone.
Wave-as-CTA-band standalone card (color, strong) merged into color_02. Redundant.

'Before' stressed-clinician stock-photo card (color, mixed) — accurate but a single generic stock-photo observation already represented by the broader stock/overlay cards (color_03, color_09); low marginal value. Cut.
Vendor/pharmacy dark-overlay-photo card (color, mixed) — duplicates the kept color_09 uniform-overlay observation; same technique, no new tell. Merge/cut.
Newsletter book-cover gradient-as-product card (color, strong) — thin; the book artifact's brand role is incidental and the palette-discipline point is already carried by color_01. Cut.
Compliance-icon mixed-tint card (color, mixed) — the claimed saturation/stroke variation is not clearly visible at this size; icons read as a uniform set. Overlaps iconography_02. Reject.
Result-row icons standalone card (iconography, mixed) merged into kept iconography_01, which covers both the problem row and the matching result row. Redundant.
Tab-bar icons-illegible card (iconography, poor) — tab icons are barely present in the tile and the wayfinding point is already made by typography_06 and layout_07. Low-value duplicate. Cut.

Homepage hero laptop-mockup card (iconography, mixed) — its own tell admits the UI is 'too small to assess craft'; the credible-mockup point is better carried by iconography_03 on the platform hero. Cut.
Newsletter book-cover-no-illustration card (iconography, poor) — flat purple rectangle with type is not meaningful iconography evidence; vague absence-of-craft. Reject.
Inventory mini-UI-panels-as-illustration card (iconography, mixed) — 'too small to read' UI screenshots are a capture/scale limitation, not assessable iconography craft. Reject.

Reporting-section no-custom-chart card (iconography, poor) — about content/feature evidence ('data promise not backed') more than visual craft; the screenshot is unreadable at scale (capture caveat). Reject.
Financial-integration unreadable-table card (iconography, poor) — duplicates the platform/tile-04 reporting complaint and rests on ~8px text legibility, a scale/capture limitation. Reject.

Wave-as-stock-3D-asset card (iconography, mixed) — duplicates the wave coverage in color_02 and asserts 'purchased stock' which is not verifiable from the tile (the wave reads as rendered/owned). Cut.

raw_cards.claim: The hero headline leans on bold weight inside a sentence ("Easily Scale", "ZERO") rather than a clear size jump to mark emphasis, so hierarchy reads as weight-toggling within one line instead of distinct levels.

faint grey "Trusted by" caption barely separating from the dark band

bold white "Apply/Onboard/Grow" labels over photo, then smaller grey paragraph

three bullets where only the first 2-3 words are bold, rest regular at the same size

several labels wrap to two lines within their narrow colored cells

raw_cards.claim: The feature cards use a consistent label-plus-body pattern (magenta bold title, grey body) that is orderly, but the magenta card titles over dark purple sit at modest contrast and read as decorative rather than crisply legible.

uniform small grey body paragraphs beneath each title

rejected_cards.reason: Hero subhead 'low contrast over busy purple field' card: the all-caps subhead and 'Trusted by' caption are actually legible white/grey on the dark band in the tile; the readability strain is overstated and the verifiable tell (weight-toggling) is already carried by typography_01. Drops to avoid a duplicate hero-typography card without a distinct visible defect.

'Is your clinic ready' three-level hierarchy card: levels are close in size but the claim is a faint mixed-competence read with no sharp visible tell beyond size proximity; merged value covered better by layout_04 (the pain-point pills) and other mixed-typography cards. Pruned to keep the calibrated set tight.

Typography 'How It Works cards' card cites tile-06, but tile-06 shows the vendor-network band and clipped logo wall, not the Apply/Onboard/Grow step cards (those are in tile-05). Tile-path/content mismatch; the real claim is kept as typography_04 against tile-05.

Typography 'vendor logo wall labels low contrast' card: the magenta tagline and white H2 are legible in the tile; this overlaps the layout_08 and color_02 logo-wall findings without adding a distinct typographic tell. Duplicate-without-new-tell.

Newsletter-block typography card: inline-bold list lead-ins are a minor, generic mixed observation already implied by layout_09 (newsletter block); not a strong enough standalone tell. Pruned for calibration.

Typography 'feature-card grid magenta-on-purple titles modest contrast' card duplicates the layout/color/iconography coverage of the same feature-card grid (layout_10, color_03, iconography_01); the contrast claim is weak in the tile (titles read clearly). Duplicate-without-new-tell.

Color 'How It Works cards consistent treatment' card cites tile-06 but the step cards are in tile-05; tile-path/content mismatch. The step-card consistency is already captured by layout_07 and typography_04.
Color 'step-card photography generic stock, no grade' card cites tile-06, but the Apply/Onboard/Grow photos are in tile-05; the cited tile shows the vendor band. Tile-path/content mismatch.

Color 'Before comparison image intentionally composited' card: flatters generic compositing competence (thin keyline, flush placement) with no standout brand-imagery tell; the same image is better used as the iconography_04 stock-photo-slider poor card. Avoids double-counting one image as both strong and poor.

Color 'first logo strip mixed marks' card duplicates color_02 (vendor logo wall) and layout_02 (trust strip) findings on the same recurring logo-strip weakness; the strongest instance is kept. Duplicate-without-new-tell.

Color 'dashboard screenshot cooler app world' card: the laptop UI in the hero tile is small and dark; the cool-vs-magenta distinction is hard to verify at this scale and overlaps layout_01's busy-hero read. Low-verifiability mixed card pruned.

Iconography '797 Compliance outline-icon set coherent' (strong) card directly conflicts with color_06 / kept set on the SAME cards which note magenta-on-magenta icons nearly disappear; keeping both a strong-coherence and the low-contrast read on identical icons would double-count. Kept the more concrete contrast finding (color_06) and layout_13.

Iconography 'problem-list icons collapse at small size' card: the four red icons are small but the 'near-illegible' read is a capture-resolution artifact more than a design tell; weak and overlaps layout_04 which praises the same row's structure. Pruned.

Iconography 'hero laptop PO screen flat screenshot' card: the PO form is legible and competently comped; the 'flat, no perspective craft' read flatters/penalizes generic screenshot presentation without a sharp tell, and overlaps typography_05/layout_10 on the same hero. Pruned for calibration.

Iconography 'laptop dashboard render unreadable rows' card: at this scroll position the laptop UI is small/dark; 'blurred into bands' is largely a capture/scale artifact rather than a design defect, and the illegible-centerpiece point is already made by layout_05. Pruned.
Iconography 'vendor blackbook logo wall clipped/ghosted' card duplicates layout_08 and color_02 on the identical logo wall; no new iconography-specific tell. Duplicate-without-new-tell.

Iconography 'Real-Time Financial Insights cards drop badge icons' card (confidence low): in tile-01 the second-row cards do show header glyphs, so the 'missing icons' claim is not verifiable in the cited tile; the icon-coverage point is already neutral. Rejected as not visibly supported.

Layout 'sticky category tab bar overlaps Reporting & Analytics' card: the overlap is real but it is the same z-index/sticky-bar collision already captured by typography_08 (tile-04) and layout_12 (tile-05 Financial Integration); this is a third duplicate of one recurring sticky-bar defect. Merged — keep two instances, drop the redundant third.
